title: Invoices
summary: Create an invoice, send it, record a payment, and chase the ones that are late.
html:
Invoices bill customers for work. Most arrive here by being generated from a job or a quote rather than typed from scratch, which is the way to do it — the lines, amounts and tracked time come across with the right descriptions already on them.

Creating one directly

Invoices → Create Invoice, pick the customer, add lines. Each line has a description, a quantity, a unit price and a tax rate. Tax is calculated per line, so an invoice mixing taxable and non-taxable items totals correctly.

A deposit line is a special case: it bills part of the amount now and leaves the rest outstanding. Whether a deposit line is taxable by default is set by deposit_task_taxable_default.

Sending it

Email Invoice sends it to the customer's primary contact, using a template you can edit under Templates. The email includes a link to view and, if you have connected a gateway, to pay it online.

Print produces the PDF. The invoice layout is a template too — see Customising for changing it without editing shipped files.

Recording a payment

Open the invoice and add a payment: amount, date, and method. An invoice is only income once a payment is recorded against it, so the finance figures and the dashboard both depend on this being kept up to date.

Payments taken online through a gateway are recorded automatically when the gateway confirms them. See Payment methods.

Part payments are fine. The invoice shows the balance outstanding until it is settled.

Overdue invoices

The dashboard lists them, and the scheduled task can email reminders — see Scheduled tasks. If reminders are not going out, the cron job is almost always the reason.

Correcting a mistake

Do not edit a sent invoice to reduce it. Raise a credit note instead, which leaves both documents in the record.
